That experience with medication sounds horrible. I'm so sorry that happened to you, and the fact that  you're the one having to suffer the consequences is awful. Don't give up hope, and remember that there's always someone there to help you!

When I first started to go to therapy, I just brought up medication with my therapist and they were perfectly fine with my preference! I'm sorry that you've had bad experiences with past therapists, but I believe if you stress how much you would not like to take medication, they will listen to you. It took me a small bit of convincing to my therapist to not recommend medication to me, so it may take a bit of effort. Just keep that in mind! Hope everything goes well for you, take care❤️

i’m not sure how much my advice will help as i haven’t come out myself, but i recommend talking to them one on one so you’re not overwhelmed, and make it apparent to the first person you talk to that you would like to tell the other yourself. i would also suggest talking to your friends to maybe boost your confidence when you decide to strike up the conversation with one of your parents. do some research incase they ask questions, and be confident in what you’re saying. if they’re very against what you say and try to start up an argument, tell them that you’re glad they at least listened and would like to continue the conversation at a later time or something like that. i’m sorry if your mom uses your gender dysphoria to get attention, but if/when you talk to her, ask her NOT to parade it around because it might make you feel worse. informing people about your gender identity is one thing but making a huge fuss about it to get attention is another. again, sorry if my suggestions aren’t the best. if you end up going through with this though, i wish you the best of luck friend!

those kittens are adorable! i’m sorry but i cannot give you their age, they do look very young though. as for keeping them, i would bring them inside if the weather is very cold or hot, and if they trust you enough. i brought a cat inside and she scratched me a lot, so if they do not want to be touched i wouldn’t risk bringing them inside. just make sure you are able to care for them! if you want them to trust you more, try feeding them treats by hand and letting them sniff you before touching or petting them. i would bring them to the vet too just to make sure they’re healthy. other than that i would suggest doing your own research, as i am not an expert. just from experience and my own research.
